title: Integration deep-dive: gateway & LlamaIndex pilot - Zenviate
summary: Discovery call focused on integrating Redwood with Zenviate's LangChain/LlamaIndex-based retrieval pipeline and evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main concerns: gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits and quotas across teams, observability hooks (tracing/request IDs/token cost), and pilot scope/timeline. AE/SE to share gateway pattern doc, rate-limit matrix, and test harness for LangChain. Next step: pilot proposal and benchmark window.

Observability hooks: traces, token cost, request IDs
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Jonah Park (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Zenviate CTO), Aisha Mohammed (Platform Eng), Ravi Patel (SRE), Marta Gomez (ML Eng)
---
[00:00] Sara Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sara from Redwood, i run the account. quick intros?
[00:12] Liam Chen: liam here, cto at zenviate, we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated then potentially private for compliance.
[00:18] Aisha Mohammed: aisha, platform eng, i'll own the integration.
[00:22] Jonah Park: jonah, se at redwood, i'll jump into the technical bits — mostly gateway patterns, skd and libraries.
[00:30] Marta Gomez: marta, ml eng, building the retrieval+llm stack with Llama Index.
[00:36] Sara Kim: great, high-level agenda: integration with your LangChain/LlamaIndex pipeline, gateway/proxy options, rate limiting/quotas, observability hooks, and pilot next steps. sound right?
[00:44] Liam Chen: yes, esp around quotas across teams and token cost visibility.
[01:05] Jonah Park: quick context question: is your runtime calling the LLM from a central gateway or do you have sidecars per service?
[01:12] Aisha Mohammed: today it's centralized through an API gateway we run, envoy + some nginx routes. we route to different downstream models depending on service.
[01:20] Jonah Park: ok that helps. two common patterns we see: 1) edge gateway proxied — your gateway forwards requests to Redwood hosted api, keep auth at edge, do fine-grained quotas and SSO; 2) internal service calls directly into Redwood SDKs (we have python/node/sdk) and you run a lightweight proxy for multi-tenant mapping. both work; choice depends on network topology and compliance.
[01:38] Ravi Patel: for private deployments, do we need VPC peering or do you support private endpoints?
[01:44] Jonah Park: we support both. for Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem), typically we do a customer-controlled control plane and either VPN or VPC peering. for hosted, there are private endpoint options (regional) — we'll send the exact network diagram.
[02:05] Marta Gomez: on the sdk side, do you have out-of-the-box adapters for LangChain or Llama Index?
[02:11] Jonah Park: we have community and first-class adapters for LangChain and a maintained LlamaIndex connector in our python SDK. examples handle streaming, tool-calling, and the token accounting hooks. i'll share the repo link.
[02:28] Sara Kim: (note) link: https://docs.redwood.ai/integrations/langchain-llamaindex — we'll put that in follow up.
[02:36] Liam Chen: good. one wrinkle — our retrieval layer runs locally and we use LlamaIndex to fetch chunks, then we send context to the LLM. sometimes we prefetch KV cache content; curious how that affects batching and cost.
[02:52] Jonah Park: on caching: Redwood runtime has prefix/KV cache primitives — if you're prefetching context, that can reduce tokens and latency if you route to a cached model instance. but note: if your app concatenates large context windows frequently, that increases token bill. we can instrument token-level costs in traces so you can attribute cost to prompt vs retrieval.
[03:18] Aisha Mohammed: that trace instrumentation — is that via headers or SDK hooks?
[03:23] Jonah Park: both. SDK inserts request-id and token breakdown in the response metadata if you use our python SDK; for proxy setups we accept X-Request-Id and return X-Redwood-TokenCost headers. we also emit OpenTelemetry spans if you want full trace integration.
[03:40] Liam Chen: perfect. can we get a per-team quota? we have multiple product teams and want to set caps to avoid runaway costs.
[03:46] Sara Kim: yes, we support rate limiting at API key and org scopes; quotas can be per-project, per-api-key, or per-route. Jonah, can you nod to the enforcement granularity?
[03:56] Jonah Park: enforcement is token-aware. rate limits are rps/request-based, and quotas are token/month or token/day. you can set soft and hard limits and webhook notifications for near-threshold. for dedicated customers we can implement per-pool quotas at the GPU level too.
[04:14] Ravi Patel: what about burst capacity? night batch jobs could spike.
[04:18] Jonah Park: burst is configurable; hosted has burst pools with fairshare, dedicated has configurable burst windows depending on the reserved capacity plan. private can be tuned by you.
[04:31] Marta Gomez: the team uses LangChain's agents heavily — do you support streaming responses for agent tool-calls?
[04:38] Jonah Park: yes, streaming is supported in SDK and via SSE/websocket from hosted. streaming also helps reduce perceived latency for agent workflows. our LangChain example shows streaming LLM output into the agent loop.
[04:52] Liam Chen: ok so next piece: gateway architecture. we run a security gateway that inspects and rewrites headers. can that co-exist?
[04:59] Jonah Park: absolutely. common pattern: gateway authenticates inbound requests, enforces quotas, then signs/forwards to Redwood with an internal service key. For private deployments, the gateway can reach a private endpoint in your VPC. we also recommend mutual TLS for added security in private setups.
[05:14] Sara Kim: quick note on secrets/KMS — do you use customer-managed keys for private?
[05:19] Jonah Park: yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integrations for key materials; hosted supports customer-managed keys for data-at-rest and envelopes depending on tier. we'll share the security whitepaper.
[05:32] Aisha Mohammed: on observability hooks — we'd like a trace id that persists from our retrieval through to the model call and back, so we can correlate latency to which chunk caused high token counts.
[05:44] Jonah Park: that's the request-id flow — you set X-Request-Id, SDK propagates it, and all spans include ext.request_id. plus token-level breakdown fields in the JSON response. note, transcription: token breakdown might show model vs system tokens; sometimes labels get fuzzy in older SDKs — but the latest has clearer fields.
[06:06] Liam Chen: latency targets — end-to-end we need <400ms p95 for short completions, for search/retrieval flows we can accept up to 1s. what latency do you see on hosted for base models?
[06:19] Jonah Park: depends on model and seq length; for small to mid seqs our hosted p95 for curated open models is around 200–400ms for text generation (short completions). we'll run a small benchmark with your prompt set to validate. dedicated typically improves p95 by 20–40% depending on GPU and batching config.
[06:38] Marta Gomez: are there model variants that behave differently with LlamaIndex? quantized models or 8-bit?
[06:45] Jonah Park: yes, quantized/8-bit variants may change tokenization and sometimes output distribution — Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload. for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) we often recommend fp16 or 4-bit quantization but validate on your eval set.
[07:02] Liam Chen: costs — can you provide an estimate for pilot: ~5k requests/day with avg 600 input tokens and 400 output tokens?
[07:12] Sara Kim: quick back-of-envelope: that's 5k*(1000 tokens) = ~5M tokens/day — we'll send a detailed cost sheet but expect hosted to be higher per-token than dedicated if you commit. we'll include batching and cache adjustments to reduce cost.
[07:30] Ravi Patel: we'd like to run a pilot to compare hosted and dedicated perf/cost for 2 weeks. what does that look like?
[07:36] Jonah Park: typical pilot: provision a small dedicated pool for 2 weeks (or run hosted with a reserved performance bucket), run your real traffic or replay through our test harness, and produce token-level cost/latency reports. we'll provide the harness and LangChain adapter.
[07:52] Aisha Mohammed: about SDK auth rotation — we manage api keys centrally and rotate weekly; how disruptive is rotation?
[07:59] Jonah Park: API key rotation is straightforward — we support multi-key rollout (grace period) and JWKS-based SSO can be used for short-lived tokens. we'll provide guidance for zero-downtime rotation.
[08:14] Liam Chen: a risk question — if hosted has an outage, can we automatically failover to another model variant or region?
[08:23] Jonah Park: yes, smart routing + fallback policies implemented in the platform let you route to a compatible variant (e.g., smaller quantized model) or a different region. you can define fallbacks per-route.
[08:34] Sara Kim: can we talk about how LangChain agents will call your API — direct SDK vs gateway? which is less work?
[08:42] Jonah Park: if you already have a gateway that injects auth and enforces quotas, calling via gateway keeps your security posture unchanged — agent processes call your gateway. If you want feature-rich telemetry and lower integration effort, using Redwood SDK directly in the agent gives better metadata (token breakdown, spans). the LangChain adapter we provide wraps our SDK and exposes the same interfaces.
[09:05] Marta Gomez: what about LlamaIndex connectors? Any gotchas for chunking or embedding calls?
[09:11] Jonah Park: embeddings are separate endpoints; bulk embeddings are recommended for indexing. watch out for tokenization mismatches between your chunker and model tokenizer — we can provide tokenizer utilities in the SDK to align chunk sizes and avoid off-by-bytes.
[09:28] Liam Chen: concerning rate-limits per team — can we have dynamic quotas that change by time of day? e.g., higher during business hours, lower at night?
[09:37] Jonah Park: yes, scheduling windows for quotas is supported through our policy API — you can set time-based overrides. we'll include policy examples in the doc.
[09:46] Aisha Mohammed: on observability exports — you mentioned OpenTelemetry, can we export to Datadog traces?
[09:53] Jonah Park: yes, we can emit OTLP to your collector; we've got examples for Datadog and Lightstep. also we emit event hooks for token-spend which can be shipped to metrics backends.
[10:06] Sara Kim: quick demo plan idea: jonah can share a LangChain example that streams responses into an agent and emits spans; we can run your prompt set through that.
[10:16] Jonah Park: i'll drop a repo with a docker-compose that simulates your gateway + langchain agent hitting redwood. there'll be env vars for api key vs service token.
[10:26] Liam Chen: ok, about compliance — SOC2 and audit logs, how granular are the logs? we need per-request auditable logs for enterprise.
[10:34] Jonah Park: audit logs include request id, api key, model used, token counts, and timestamps. for Private we can give longer retention and enterprise logging options. hosted has configurable retention windows.
[10:45] Ravi Patel: are prompts stored? for debugging we sometimes need to see the prompt but we need controls for redaction.
[10:52] Jonah Park: retention and redaction policies are configurable; by default we retain minimal metadata, but you can opt into full retention with access controls. private deployments allow you to keep everything in your network.
[11:07] Marta Gomez: any suggestions for reducing cost for RAG workloads?
[11:12] Jonah Park: common levers: 1) aggressive prefix/KV cache for repeated context, 2) embedding-only retrieval to minimize tokens in generation, 3) quantized model variants for cheaper per-token cost, 4) batching and async pipelines where possible, 5) set soft quotas and alerts. Redwood Optimize can make automated suggestions after initial pilot.
[11:36] Liam Chen: can we get an example of the header flows for request id and token cost in proxy?
[11:40] Jonah Park: example: client -> your gateway (sets X-Request-Id) -> gateway forwards X-Request-Id + Authorization: Bearer <service-key> -> redwood responds with X-Redwood-TokenCost: "input:120,output:230,total:350" and our json includes token_meta. we'll paste exact shapes in the doc.
[12:05] Sara Kim: i'm going to summarize next steps now and then open q/a.
[12:09] Sara Kim: to recap — we'll send: gateway integration doc, langchain/llamaindex example repo, pilot proposal and pricing, and a short network diagram for private options. you (liam) will send prompt set and pod topology. agree?
[12:20] Liam Chen: yes.
[12:22] Aisha Mohammed: question — if we do dedicated, how long to provision? we can't wait weeks.
[12:27] Jonah Park: small dedicated pools can be provisioned in 48–72 hours if capacity exists; we'll confirm availability. for larger reserved commitments it's longer.
[12:37] Marta Gomez: will the SDK auto-handle token accounting if we stream?
[12:41] Jonah Park: yes, streaming responses include incremental token counts and final totals in the metadata. older language may show slight off-by-ones but it's accurate on the latest sdk.
[12:54] Ravi Patel: are there any known issues with quantized models + streaming? sometimes we see truncated outputs.
[13:02] Jonah Park: truncated outputs can happen with specific tokenizers and quantization; it's model-specific. we'll run your eval set on the quantized variants during the pilot to check for regressions.
[13:18] Liam Chen: what's the legal procurement path? we may need SOC2 + DPA before production.
[13:24] Sara Kim: Redwood's enterprise team can engage; we have a standard DPA and SOC2 attestation. i'll loop in enterprise sales if procurement is needed.
[13:33] Aisha Mohammed: question about testing locally — can our devs run a local mock of redwood for integration tests?
[13:38] Jonah Park: we provide a lightweight local shim in the sdk that mocks responses; for more realistic tests we recommend using a staged hosted environment we spin up for the pilot.
[13:50] Liam Chen: metrics — we'll want per-route cost dashboards. can you export token spend per route to our grafana?
[13:57] Jonah Park: yes, we have a metrics export pipeline. we'll provide a prometheus endpoint or pushgateway integration that maps routes to token spend.
[14:10] Sara Kim: ok wrapping up, any last concerns?
[14:16] Marta Gomez: just one: LlamaIndex connector — will it handle embeddings batching automatically?
[14:21] Jonah Park: our connector batches embeddings and you can configure batch sizes; we'll include the defaults and how to tune for latency vs throughput.
[14:33] Ravi Patel: security follow-up: i'll want a short list of network ports and mTLS cert formats.
[14:39] Jonah Park: noted — i'll include a network checklist.
[14:45] Sara Kim: thanks all. we'll send follow-up materials and book the pilot kickoff.
[14:50] Liam Chen: appreciate it. this was helpful.
[14:54] Sara Kim: end of call.
---
